segments.text: Five numbers. One pyramid. How large can we make the top?
Place one to five along the bottom. Each box adds the three closest boxes below it.
Follow the centre number. It appears in all three middle sums.
So it reaches the top three times.
The neighbours count twice. Each end counts only once.
Put five in the centre, three and four beside it, and one and two at the ends.
A larger number earns more in a position that counts more. That is why this arrangement is best.
The middle row becomes nine, twelve and eleven. Add them: thirty-two.
Answer C. Count how often each number contributes.
